title: Finite covers of projective schemes are projective
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $p:T\to S$ be projective in the global closed-embedding convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism], and let $h:Y\to T$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $p\circ h$ is locally projective in the following explicit sense: for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, with $T_U=p^{-1}(U)$ and $Y_U=(p\circ h)^{-1}(U)$, there exist $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $Y_U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_U$ over $U$. Thus $Y_U\to U$ is projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. In particular, if $S$ is affine, $Y\to S$ is projective. No global projective-space embedding is asserted when $S$ is arbitrary.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$. Choose the global embedding $T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ supplied by [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Restrict it to the inverse image of $U$. The affine-quotient description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] still holds on every affine open of this open subscheme of the target, so the restriction $T_U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$ is closed. The base-change presentation [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] identifies this target with $\mathbf P^n_U$, whose relative-Proj chart interface is [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. The restricted map $h_U:Y_U\to T_U$ is finite: on each affine open of $T_U$, which is also an affine open of $T$, its inverse image and finite ring map are exactly those in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For every affine open $W\subseteq U$, the $n+1$ standard projective charts over $W$ cover $\mathbf P^n_W$, and their inverse images in $T_W$ are affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $T_W$ is a finite union of quasi-compact affine opens. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $T_U\to U$ is quasi-compact. Together with the restricted closed embedding, this proves it is projective under the stated convention.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: work over an affine open of S

proof.text: The morphism $T_U\to U$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], and $h_U$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Their composite $f_U:Y_U\to U$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] it is of finite type. Thus [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] supplies local finite type and quasi-compactness; since $U$ itself is affine, $Y_U=f_U^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact.

Let $a:Y_U\to\mathbf P^n_U$ be the embedding of $T_U$ composed with $h_U$, and put $\mathcal L=a^*\mathcal O(1)$. The twist is invertible by its glued free rank-one presentation [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and its pullback is invertible by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. For each homogeneous coordinate $x_i$, the formulas $x_i=(x_i/x_j)e_j$ on the standard chart $D_+(x_j)$ define a global section of $\mathcal O(1)$: on overlaps this follows from $e_j=(x_j/x_k)e_k$, the transition rule in [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Write $s_i=a^*x_i$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: coordinate sections and their corresponding pullback sections on Y; Modules Tags 0B8L and 0098

proof.text: The standard chart $D_+(x_i)$ over $U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A[x_j/x_i:j\ne i]$: a degree-zero fraction $F/x_i^d$, with $F$ homogeneous of degree $d$, is a sum of terms $c\prod_{j\ne i}(x_j/x_i)^{a_j}$ after cancelling the power of $x_i$; conversely every monomial in the ratios has such a homogeneous numerator [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $T_i=T_U\cap D_+(x_i)$ is affine, with coordinate ring a quotient of that polynomial ring. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $V_i=h_U^{-1}(T_i)$ is affine. These finitely many opens cover $Y_U$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] identifies the value of $s_i$ at $y$ with $x_i(a(y))\otimes1$; on a chart $D_+(x_j)$ containing $a(y)$, its value is $(x_i/x_j)(a(y))e_j$. This is nonzero exactly when $x_i$ is absent from the homogeneous prime representing $a(y)$, that is, when $a(y)\in D_+(x_i)$. A nonzero vector remains nonzero under the residue-field extension $\kappa(a(y))\to\kappa(y)$ (identify the one-dimensional space with its field). Thus $(Y_U)_{s_i}=V_i$. Together with the quasi-compactness in step 2, the sections $s_i$ (all of power one) satisfy both conditions in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Hence $\mathcal L$ is ample on $Y_U$.

source.place: Tag 01PS (definition-ample); affine charts from Constructions 01NF; pullback fibres from Sheaves 0098

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] to the ring $A$, the locally finite type morphism $f_U:Y_U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of step 2, and the invertible ample module $\mathcal L$ of steps 3–4. It gives $N\geq0$ and an immersion $v:Y_U\to\operatorname{Proj}(A[z_0,\ldots,z_N])=\mathbf P^N_U$ over $U$. We use only its immersion and structure-map equation, not its additional twist-isomorphism clause. This packages precisely the clearing-denominators and chart-generator argument of the imported proof.

Projective space $\mathbf P^N_U$ is separated over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Its composite with $v$ is the proper $f_U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $v$ proper. It is an immersion by step 5, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. The morphism $f_U$ is quasi-compact by step 2. The embedding and this quasi-compactness are exactly [def-pc-projective-morphism], proving $Y_U\to U$ projective. As $U$ was arbitrary, the corrected local assertion follows. For affine $S$, take $U=S$.
